models.observations: The broad hide canopy, red panels and pennant read cleanly. The secondary lodge is hidden behind the main eave and the 64-pixel outline reads like Dawn, with no obvious mudbrick or copper feature. Serialized LOD counts 1322/650/335 passed the package validator.
defects: Expose a stepped mudbrick civic annex or copper-capped drum tower beyond a visible eave, with its base and roof readable together at 64 pixels, to separate Bronze from Dawn.

models.observations: The dark hide cone and broad gray masonry wing establish a heavier stronghold; the paired ivory horns remain visible against sky at 64 pixels. Two red-skinned signal drums flank a timber gateway. Serialized LOD counts 1095/519/268 passed the package validator.

Low swept hide gores meet a distinct timber vestibule. Two painted drums, the mallets on the larger head and the swallowtail signal flag explain the hall's public role. The gold cap and red sectors remain visible at 64 pixels. Serialized LOD counts 906/414/227 passed the package validator.

The high dark slate cone breaks into distinct courses above a tall rough-stone wall; the dark projecting vestibule retains its ivory tusk contrast against that wall. The height and deep skirt separate this from the earlier low halls. Serialized LOD counts 1288/616/335 passed the package validator.

The broad terracotta crown on pale plaster reads warmer and fuller than the Medieval slate hall; an orange entry canopy, festival pennant, horn posts and laced musicians' drums remain legible in the front view. Serialized LOD counts 1356/684/335 passed the package validator.

The light masonry and terracotta read correctly, but two blue-gray slivers interrupt the roof field with no visible shaft, making the small towers read like pieces clipping through the roof surface. Serialized LOD counts 1242/648/311 passed the package validator.
defects: Reposition the secondary towers or portico to show complete masonry shafts and crowns above or beyond the tiled eaves. Eliminate the disconnected cap fragments in the normal preview.

models.observations: The pearl roofs, twin gold finials and cyan open crown separate this age immediately at 64 pixels. The crown struts meet its rim, and the retained drum gate and red paint tie it visibly to earlier halls. Serialized LOD counts 1470/804/419 passed the package validator.

A tall narrow antenna tower at the left and an asymmetrical blue glass roof define the information-age silhouette. The red panel, dark pennant and round marching drums still identify the clan hall against the blue. Serialized LOD counts 1033/519/276 passed the package validator.

The low steel-colored roof is visibly distinct from the pitched preindustrial halls, but its paired squat pods end in peach flat plugs. The gray wall and roof lack a strong modern civic detail at thumbnail size. Serialized LOD counts 1174/580/311 passed the package validator.
defects: Replace the peach pod tops with clearly built vents or clerestories and give the wall or pod a substantial glazed band with steel mullions that reads against the roof at 64 pixels.

models.observations: A red-brick exhaust stack grows from the ground at the left of the soot-gray metal roof. Its broad dark mouth clears the skyline; the contrasting red-striped eave and two hide drums remain legible in the low silhouette. Serialized LOD counts 1151/569/281 passed the package validator.
The lateral stepped brick annex now clears the eave. Its gold cap and stepped footprint are readable at 64 pixels and uniquely mark Bronze beside Dawn. Revalidated LOD counts 1018/516/275.

Complete masonry shafts rise from substantial bases into terracotta caps outside the hall. Both crowns are clearly tied to towers, and the bone crest, door and two drums stay unobstructed. Revalidated LOD counts 1340/730/351.

Blue glazed bands and steel caps now finish both concrete pods. Their junctions with the broad low council roof read cleanly at phone size; the original paired drums and horn crest retain the Orc civic identity. Revalidated LOD counts 1328/726/331.

Both white-gold towers remain visually grounded with their new spacing. The continuous cyan halo and its supporting crown remain visible and well separated from the pale roof. Revalidated LOD counts 1470/804/419.
